reading.title: Who can you trust online?
reading.text: Fake news spreads incredibly fast, often faster than the truth. Researchers have found that false stories are shared most often by credulous readers who do not check the source. To be credible, a report should name its sources and the credentials of the experts it quotes. Several platforms now label posts from unreliable websites, and they deserve some credit for this. However, critics say that labels alone cannot restore the credibility of journalism, and that schools must teach young people how to judge information for themselves.
